approach: Find the heat needed to bring all the ice to boiling water at 100 °C, then check how much steam must condense to supply exactly that heat, since the mixture cannot rise above 100 °C while steam is still present.

steps.text: Find the heat needed to warm the ice to 0 °C, melt it, and then heat the resulting water to 100 °C.
Find the heat released if all the steam were to condense at 100 °C.
steps.why_this_step: Latent heat of vaporisation is 540 cal g⁻¹, and condensation releases it without any temperature change.

steps.text: Since 13500 cal is more than the 10260 cal needed, the mixture reaches 100 °C before all the steam condenses, so only part of the steam condenses and the mixture stays at 100 °C.
steps.equation: Let x g of steam condense: x × 540 = 10260

steps.text: Solve for x and find the remaining steam.
The water present is the melted ice plus the condensed steam.

final_answer.value: 73 g water at 100 °C and 6 g steam at 100 °C

common_mistakes.text: Assuming all 25 g of steam condenses and the mixture then cools further gives a temperature above 100 °C, which is impossible, because full condensation releases more heat than the ice needs to reach 100 °C.
